theme: Awesome lists and curated catalogues: awesome-public-datasets, awesome-alternative-data, awesome-quant data, awesome-economics, awesome-tourism, awesome-real-estate, awesome-transportation-data

candidates.name: uber-tlc-foil-response
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed data from FiveThirtyEight's NYC TLC FOIL request: 4.5M Uber pickups Apr-Sep 2014 (six monthly CSVs, lat/lon + base code), 14.3M Jan-Jun 2015 Uber pickups (uber-raw-data-janjune-15.csv.zip, dispatching base/date/location ID), trip-level files for 10 other for-hire-vehicle companies, aggregated daily pickups for 329 FHV companies (Aggregate_FHV_Data.xlsx), Uber-Jan-Feb-FOIL.csv. NYC only, 2014-2015, 9 commits, well-known/stable, no explicit license stated.
candidates.why_useful: A city-level ground-transport activity proxy of the kind gap 10 asks for (airport/ground transport capacity and traffic); mainly useful as a worked example of NYC TLC/FHV data structure rather than current data (2014-15 vintage) - would need the live TLC portal for present quarters.

candidates.name: skytrax-reviews-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Four committed CSVs scraped from airlinequality.com (Skytrax): 41,396 airline reviews, 17,721 airport reviews, 2,264 lounge reviews, 1,258 seat reviews, with rating dimensions (comfort, cleanliness, staff, amenities). Scraped as of Aug 2, 2015. CC0-1.0 license on the repo (scrape legality of underlying site noted as ambiguous by author). 73 stars/41 forks.
candidates.why_useful: Text/sentiment travel-demand proxy adjacent to Airbnb (traveler experience/sentiment on air travel) - could feed a text-based travel-demand sentiment index (gap 14 adjacent) though it is a one-time 2015 scrape, not updated, so limited as a current indicator; more useful as a methodology template for scraping airline-review sentiment than as current data.

candidates.name: BailleurVerif - French Non-Compliant Rental Listings Observatory
candidates.what_it_holds: Time-stamped, longitudinal dataset on data.gouv.fr (French government open-data portal) tracking short-term rental listings in France found non-compliant with local registration/regulation rules (an 'observatory' feed maintained by BailleurVerif). Cataloged in awesomedata/awesome-public-datasets under Government (BailleurVerif.yml).
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-point for gap 12 (STR ordinance trackers / city registration datasets) for France, which the CONTEXT gap list names as a target geography (France STR registration) but we don't yet hold a France-specific compliance/registration series; a longitudinal non-compliance count could proxy enforcement intensity and registered-listing counts over time.
candidates.time_coverage: ongoing, dated snapshots (exact start unclear from listing)
candidates.size_hint: unknown row count; time-stamped longitudinal series
candidates.license: French open-data licence (Licence Ouverte, per data.gouv.fr defaults)

candidates.name: thailand-housing-prices
candidates.what_it_holds: Clean, committed Thailand and Bangkok residential property price indexes per the awesome-public-datasets Economics entry (kesar/thailand-housing-prices). Regional (Thailand/Bangkok) housing price time series.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal APAC housing-supply-economics data point relevant to gap 13 (long-term rental/housing crossover) and gap 7 (APAC regional travel/housing) but Thailand is not one of Airbnb's largest markets for ABNB KPI forecasting; low direct relevance, flagged for completeness.
candidates.time_coverage: unspecified, appears current as of README

candidates.name: gtfs-hub
candidates.what_it_holds: Aggregation/enhancement pipeline for German public transit GTFS feeds, gathered from CUTR-at-USF/awesome-transit list. Produces enhanced GTFS feeds for German transit agencies.
candidates.why_useful: A one-command pull method for German ground-transport capacity data (gap 10 mentions DB/rail capacity generally); minor incremental value since it's a processing pipeline for transit schedules, not passenger volumes.

candidates.name: The Mobility Database (GTFS catalogue)
candidates.what_it_holds: Repository/catalogue of 2000+ mobility (transit GTFS) datasets worldwide, successor to OpenMobilityData; linked from CUTR-at-USF/awesome-transit on GitHub. Not itself a GitHub-hosted data store but a discovery index for transit schedule/GTFS feeds globally, many of which are mirrored on GitHub by individual agencies/maintainers.
candidates.why_useful: A discovery tool (like the CKAN/Socrata discovery clients gap 17 asks for) to find ground-transportation capacity data by city/country as an ABNB travel-volume cross-check; breadth is high but each underlying feed needs individual vetting.

candidates.name: awesome-public-datasets
candidates.what_it_holds: The master curated catalogue itself (auto-generated from awesomedata/apd-core YAML metadata files), organized into ~35 sections (Agriculture, Economics, Finance, GIS, Government, SocialNetworks, SocialSciences, Transportation, etc.), each with dozens to hundreds of dataset links, mostly to external hosts (many recently-added entries are small commercial SEO-style 'open dataset' pages rather than research-grade data - the catalogue quality has degraded with many low-value submissions circa 2026, alongside legitimate long-standing entries like OpenFlights, RITA/BTS TranStat, Skytrax reviews, and Uber TLC data).
candidates.why_useful: Serves as a standing discovery index worth periodic re-scanning (per gap 17's spirit of open-data discovery tooling), but as of this pass it surfaced no committed Airbnb/STR/tourism-specific datasets beyond what is separately flagged; most new entries are unrelated commercial price-index microsites.
candidates.size_hint: hundreds of linked datasets across 35 sections
candidates.license: CC0 for the list itself; varies per linked dataset

candidates.name: awesome-transit
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated list of transit-data resources: Mobility Database, Transitland, National Transit Database (US), transport.data.gouv.fr (France), sample-gtfs-feed test data, CapMetrics (Austin historical transit vehicle positions, github.com/scascketta/CapMetrics), Bus Observatory real-time vehicle-movement archive API, mfdz/gtfs-hub, Citylines.co.
candidates.why_useful: Discovery index for ground-transport capacity/ridership data (gap 10); CapMetrics specifically gives an Austin-specific historical transit archive, a market already in our Inside Airbnb 13-city panel, so could be a local travel-activity cross-check for that city.

candidates.name: CapMetrics
candidates.what_it_holds: Historical archive of Austin, TX transit (Capital Metro) vehicle position/ridership-adjacent data, per its listing in CUTR-at-USF/awesome-transit. Austin is one of the 13 cities in our Inside Airbnb panel.
candidates.why_useful: A local ground-transport activity series for Austin that could be cross-checked against Inside Airbnb Austin listings/calendar activity as a market-level travel-volume proxy (gap 10), though scope and freshness need verification before use.

candidates.name: OpenFlights airport/airline/route database
candidates.what_it_holds: Static reference tables of world airports, airlines, and routes (not schedules/volumes), maintained as flat files linkable from GitHub mirrors; catalogued in awesomedata/awesome-public-datasets/Transportation. Widely mirrored on GitHub (e.g. jpatokal/openflights).
candidates.why_useful: A reference/join table (airport-to-city, route existence) rather than a volume series; could support building an airline-capacity proxy for gap 10 when paired with a real traffic source (e.g. BTS T-100), but on its own has no time-series volume.
